headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a tuple of strings (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

I’m afraid I don’t have a live database of current showtimes or film runtimes at hand, so I can’t pull up a definitive list of movies that meet those exact criteria right now. However, here’s a practical way to find what you’re looking for: | Step | What to do | Why it works | |------|------------|--------------| | 1 | **Choose a theater close to Times Square** – the most common ones are
• AMC Empire 25 (Broadway & 42nd St)
• Regal Cinemas Times Square (Broadway & W 34th St)
• Alamo Drafthouse Cinema (Broadway & W 34th St) | These venues are literally within a few blocks of Times Square, so you’ll be able to walk there in under 10 minutes. | | 2 | **Check each theater’s online schedule** – visit their official site or a ticket‑booking platform (Fandango, AMC.com, Regal.com, etc.). | Most sites let you filter by “Showtime” and display the runtime next to each film. | | 3 | **Filter for films ≤ 120 minutes** – look for titles marked “Short” or “Feature” with a runtime listed. | The runtime is usually shown in the film description; you can also click the title to see details. | | 4 | **Book a ticket** – once you’ve found a film that fits the length requirement, reserve a seat. | Booking online guarantees you a spot and lets you confirm the exact start time. | ### Quick example (using AMC’s site) 1. Go to [AMC.com](https://www.amc.com/) and search for “New York, NY”. 2. Select “AMC Empire 25” from the list of nearby locations. 3. Browse the day’s schedule; runtimes appear in parentheses after the title (e.g., *“The Grand Budapest Hotel (99 min)”*). 4. Click on a film that shows a runtime of 90–120 minutes and proceed to purchase tickets. If you prefer a single‑stop solution, you can try a quick Google search like: ``` "movies playing near Times Square today with runtime under 2 hours" ``` Google often pulls up a carousel of theaters with showtimes and runtimes directly in the search results. --- #### Bottom line While I can’t pull up a live list for you, the steps above will get you a short‑film (≤ 2 hours) that’s within walking distance of Times Square in just a few clicks. Happy watching!
